summary: Pierce County L-4 lookout built in 1954 and removed or destroyed in 1972; the summit was logged around 2014 and the footings are visible on permit-only timberland.

facts.design: Wooden L-4 cab tower; FFLOS and firelookout.com say 40 feet, a biennial report quoted by Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb says 20 feet
facts.status_note: Removed in 1972 per FFLOS; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed that year. Summit logged around 2014.

access.note: Private timberland. WillhiteWeb's 2016 visit found a permit required from Hancock Forest Management, and says ownership and rules likely changed. Gravel road.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The footings are set to one side and visible, per the 2016 visit. A permit is required.

events.note: Forestry Division biennial report calls a lookout on the site urgently needed and says a new road is partly built
40-foot wooden L-4 tower built in 1954 per FFLOS and firelookout.com; a later report describes 20 feet
Removed per FFLOS; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed

Summit logged around 2014; slash buried much of what could have been lookout structure
WillhiteWeb site visit; footings set to one side and visible; permit required on private timberland

corrections.why: The Register and firelookout.com both give a 40-foot tower. The 6.1 m in the record matches the 20-foot figure from the biennial report, which WillhiteWeb calls too short.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com give 40 feet; Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb quote a biennial report giving 20 feet, which Willhite calls short and thinks was 30 or 40 feet.
The Register says removed in 1972; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year agrees.
The Register lists the state Division of Forestry/DNR as administrator; WillhiteWeb's 2016 visit found private timberland that needed a permit.

sources.title: St. Paul Lookout - Kapowsin Tree Farm

notes_for_editor: No staffing or fire records for this lookout turned up in the pages read or in two searches, so staffing and fires are left out. Height is contested: the correction proposes 12.2 m (40 ft) from FFLOS and firelookout.com, while the 20-foot figure comes from a biennial report that Willhite doubts. Access is permission-only per the 2016 WillhiteWeb visit and may be out of date.
